[2.0] The brief facts leading to filing of present appeal are as follows:

sentences.text: [2.1] On 29.05.2011 at about 09.00 PM, the appellant was going as a NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2036/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined pedestrian from Tarapur towards Mohansinh Chotubhai Rathwa Arts College to attend his duty as watchman and at that time the opponent No.1 came on wrong side by driving his Motorcycle bearing No.GJ-06- EA-3427 in excessive speed, rashly and in negligent manner and hit his motorcycle with the appellant, as a result of which the appellant was thrown on the road and sustained grievous injuries resulting into permanent partial disability.
Therefore, the original claimant filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.10 lakh.

[2.2] After considering the evidence produced on record by the respective parties,
learned Tribunal has been pleased to hold the original opponent No.1 - driver of offending motorcycle to be solely negligent for the accident and awarded compensation of Rs.4,05,500/-.
Hence, present First Appeal is filed by the appellant - original claimant for enhancement of compensation.
[3.0] Though served, respondent Nos.1 and 2 have chosen not to appear before the Court.

[4.0] Learned advocate Mr. R.G. Dwivedi appearing for the appellant has submitted that the learned Tribunal has committed an error in considering only 60% disability body as a whole against 70% physical disability however, the claimant has sustained 100% functional disability and that the learned Tribunal has taken a view contrary to the decision of the coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Bhikhabhai Manilal Patel reported in 2010 (1) GLR 699.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further submitted that the learned Tribunal committed an error in considering monthly income of the appellant only at Rs.13,000/- and even no compensation is awarded under the head of future loss of income.

He has further submitted that even under the head of pain, shock and suffering only NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2036/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Rs.25,000/- is awarded and in view of number of surgeries performed on the appellant, learned Tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.2,50,000/- under the head of pain, shock and suffering.
Therefore, he has requested to allow the appeal.

[5.0] Learned advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati appearing for the respondent No.3 - insurance company has opposed the First Appeal on the ground that no error is committed by the learned Tribunal in considering that there is no loss of income to the claimant as his income continued to increased even after his sustaining disability.

He has relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajkumar vs.
Ajaykumar & Ors. reported in (2011)1 SCC 343.

[7.0] Having heard learned advocate for the appellant - insurance company and learned advocate for the original claimant and perusing the record, it appears that the learned Tribunal has considered the evidence produced and adduced by both the parties including the affidavit of the claimant (Exh.17), complaint (Exh.20A),
panchnama of scene of accident (Exh.20B), charge-sheet (Exh.20H) as well as the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi vs. H.R.S.T.C.
reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819 and Parmeshwari Devi vs. Amir Chand reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, wherein it is held that it is settled law that negligence is required to be proved in claim petition under section 166 of the MV Act only on the touchstone of the preponderance of probability and not beyond doubt and learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2036/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Tribunal has held the driver of offending motorcycle to be solely negligent for the accident.
Even otherwise, negligence and liability is not challenged by the learned advocate for the insurance company.
[8.0] Perusing the record & proceedings, it appears that the original claimant filed his affidavit at Exh.17, wherein he has stated that at the time of accident, he was getting salary of Rs.13,293/- p.m. by serving as Watchman in Shri Mohansinh Chottubhai Rathwa College of Arts, Pavi-Jetpur and in support of his say, the claimant has produced his salary slip (Exh.20G) for the month of May, 2011 which shows monthly income of appellant as Rs.13,293/- per month

and therefore, the learned Tribunal has rightly held the monthly income of appellant - claimant at Rs.13,000/-, which does not call for any interference.
[8.1] Learned advocate for the insurance company relying on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ajaykumar & Ors. (Supra) has submitted that there is no loss of future income to the appellant - claimant even after the accident as he was in government job and his salary increased from time to time and therefore, learned Tribunal has rightly not awarded any amount under the head of future loss of income.

But, it is needless to say that there is no rule or law that after the accident merely because income of victim of accident has increased, compensation is required to be refused towards future loss of income.
In the case of Mohd. Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain vs. Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation reported in 2022(0) AIJEL-SC 70212 relying on the decision in the case of Ajaykumar & Ors.

entities.text: Mohd. Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain vs. Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation reported in 2022(0) AIJEL-SC 70212
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (Supra), it has been held that even if the income of the claimant had increased after the accident, it would not be enough ground to disable him from claiming compensation for future prospect as the rise in income may be attributed to multiple other NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2036/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined factors and that in cases of permanent disablement caused by motor accident, the claimant is entitled to not just future loss of income but also entitled to get compensation for future prospects.

The just compensation must be interpreted in such a manner as to place the claimant in the same position as he was before the Ganpatbhai Bhagabhai Rathwa vs Arvindbhai Somabhai Rathwa on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44273068/
3 accident took place.

entities.text: Ganpatbhai Bhagabhai Rathwa vs Arvindbhai Somabhai Rathwa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Merely because the income of the claimant has shown an upward trend after the accident, the same cannot be a ground to refuse the claim for compensation or future prospects.
[8.2] If the claimant not sustained such permanent disablement, the possibility of a higher escalation or greater increase in income in future cannot be ruled out.
Considering the nature of his work, skill, and capacity to work, such disablement is adversely affect his earning potential.
Due to the permanent disablement suffered, the progression of the claimant's income is likely to be curtailed to some extent.

Therefore, merely because the claimant's income has increased after the accident would not be sufficient ground to deny future prospects, as rise in income may be attributable to various factors and does not necessarily reflect the loss of earning capacity suffered by the claimant.
Hence, in view of the said pronouncement, the compensation assessed by the learned Tribunal is not just and proper and calls for an interference.

[8.3] Now so far as quantum is concerned, the learned Tribunal has accepted monthly income of claimant at Rs.13,000/- and found that the appellant - claimant produced permanent disability certificate at Exh.23 issued by Dr. P.P. Maniyar, Orthopedic Department, Assistant Professor, SSG Hospital, Vadodara according to which, the appellant had sustained crush injury over left leg with fracture compound tibia fibula and crush injury of knee and lower limb amputation was NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2036/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined performed.
The said doctor has assessed 70% permanent disability of left leg.

However, the learned advocate appearing for the respective parties before the learned Tribunal submitted a pursis (Exh.24) indicating their mutual agreement to accept 60% permanent disability of body as a whole.
Hence, once the disablement is accepted, same is not required to be interfered with.

[8.4] Further, the birth date of the claimant as per the injury certificate (Exh.22) and disability certificate (Exh.23) is mentioned as 01.06.1974 and therefore, at the time of accident, the claimant was aged 36 years.

Hence, in view of decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. [2009 (6) SCC 121], the claimant was in the age group of 36 to 40 and is entitled to multiplier of 15 and in view of decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, as the appellant - claimant was in permanent government job, is entitled to 50%
addition towards future prospects and therefore, monthly future income would come to Rs.19,500 [Rs.13,000 + Rs.6500 (50% of Rs.13,000)] and applying disability of 60% body as a whole

[8.5] It has also come on record before the learned Tribunal that the appellant - original claimant remained on leave for 365 days due to the injury and disability sustained by him in the vehicular accident and therefore, the learned Tribunal relying on the decision of the coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation V/s Kamlaben Valjibhai Vora and Ors.

reported in 2001(3) GLR 2528 has awarded Rs.1,56,000/- (Rs.13,000 x 12) towards actual loss of income, which in the considered opinion of this Court, does not call for any interference, as leaves are deducted from the balance leave of employee and claimant was entitled to encash such leave at the time of superannuation.
[8.6] Further, the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,74,268/- towards medical treatment and medicines as per the list produced at Exh.20 and Rs.25,000/- towards transportation, special diet and attendant charges, which does not call for any interference considering the nature of injury and disability sustained by the appellant - original claimant.

But, the compensation of Rs.25,000/-
under the head of pain, shock and suffering as awarded by the learned Tribunal is too meager in view of the 60% permanent disability body as a whole sustained by the claimant and therefore, same is reassessed at Rs.1,50,000/-.

Further, the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- under the head of loss of amenities however, this Court is of considered opinion that in view of serious disability sustained by the claimant, it would be just and proper to award Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.

Thus, total compensation of Rs.4,05,500/- as awarded by the learned Tribunal is on lower side, for the reasons recorded hereinabove, and therefore, same is reassessed as Rs.27,11,500/- and hence,
the appellant - original claimant is entitled to get additional amount of Rs.23,06,000/-
(Rs.27,11,500 - Rs.4,05,500) towards compensation and therefore, the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is required to be modified to the aforesaid extent.

[9.1] It is needless to say that the Motor Vehicles Act is a benevolent legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims, or their families and there is no bar that compensation is restricted up to the claim by the claimant and the High Court and Tribunal have to award the compensation up to that extent.

In this regard reference is required to be made to the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nagappa Vs Gurudayal Singh and others, reported in (2003) 2 Supreme Court Cases 274, wherein, it has been observed that there is no restriction that compensation could be awarded only up to the amount claimed by the claimant.
